verdict.rationale: Google DeepMind publishes a model card for the flagship Gemini 4 Argon with a dedicated "Evaluation" section, and the Safety & Security section describes red-teaming and automated evaluation approaches alongside published results tables. That is a first-party channel for evaluation claims. However, nothing in the evidence shows that benchmark claims come with eval names, settings, harnesses or prompts needed to reproduce or audit them. Missing for 10: documented eval names and settings per benchmark claim, published harness or prompt details, evidence that the reported numbers can be reproduced, independent audit of the methodology.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, published benchmark claims come with enough methodology — eval names, settings, harness or prompts — that I could reproduce or at least audit them

citations.quote: Sections: Model Information, Model Data (training dataset), Implementation and Sustainability, Distribution, Evaluation, Intended Usage and Limitations, Safety & Security.
Automated Red Teaming to dynamically evaluate Gemini for safety and security considerations at scale, complementing human red teaming and static evaluations
